## Load packages

`clusterProfiler` runs the enrichment and `enrichplot` draws it; `enrichVolcano` (the user's own
package, not on CRAN) is called with `::` for its label cleaner.

```{r setup}
pacman::p_load(here, dplyr, purrr, stringr, ggplot2, readxl, clusterProfiler, enrichplot)
here::i_am("03_Pathway_Enrichment/08_pathway_maps/a_script/08_pathway_maps.qmd")
```

## Read inputs

Pathway maps of the two training responses: which pathways each leg moves, how they cluster by
shared proteins, and which proteins link them. Figures only: every test and table stays in
`01_run_fgsea_and_fry`. Adapted from Sam's PR #26 (sc-norton).

Three inputs: `protein_results` and `set_tests` from `01_run_fgsea_and_fry` (per-protein
statistics per contrast, and per-set results), and the gene sets from `00_build_gene_sets`.

```{r read}
stage <- here("03_Pathway_Enrichment", "08_pathway_maps")
book <- here(
  "03_Pathway_Enrichment", "01_run_fgsea_and_fry", "c_data", "01_run_fgsea_and_fry.xlsx"
)
protein_results <- read_excel(book, "protein_results")
set_tests <- read_excel(book, "set_tests")
sets <- readRDS(here("03_Pathway_Enrichment", "00_build_gene_sets", "c_data", "gene_sets.rds"))
arms <- c(BFR = "BFR_Post-Pre", HLRT = "HLRT_Post-Pre")
```

## Rank the proteins

The same ranking `01` used: for each training contrast, the selected proteins' moderated t
statistics, named by gene and sorted from largest to smallest.

```{r ranked}
ranked <- map(arms, function(cn) {
  with(filter(protein_results, contrast == cn, selected), sort(set_names(t, gene), TRUE))
})
lengths(ranked)
map(ranked, function(x) head(x, 3))
```

`labels` gives every set a readable name for the figures.

```{r labels}
labels <- set_tests |>
  distinct(set_id, database, pathway) |>
  mutate(label = enrichVolcano::clean_label(pathway, width = 1000))
```

## Choose the pathways to draw

The main sets `01` kept, one per cluster of overlapping sets, significant at FDR < 0.05 in either
leg. GO:BP has 73 and Reactome 31, so each is cut to the 30 with the smallest adjusted p.

```{r drawn}
drawn <- set_tests |>
  filter(method == "fgsea", contrast %in% arms, padj < 0.05, main) |>
  summarise(padj = min(padj), .by = c(set_id, database)) |>
  slice_min(padj, n = 30, by = database, with_ties = FALSE) |>
  left_join(select(labels, set_id, label), by = "set_id")
count(drawn, database)
```

## Run the enrichment

enrichplot's maps need a clusterProfiler result object, so `compareCluster()` runs GSEA on both
rankings at once, with the same sets, size limits and rankings as `01`. clusterProfiler 4.20 runs
GSEA through enrichit, whose multilevel algorithm is derived from fgsea's but is separate code, so
the check below compares its normalised enrichment scores (NES) with `01`'s. `run_gsea()` runs once
per collection, and the check and the maps both read the results in `compared`. The seed is set
right before each call, so the permutations are the same on every run.

```{r run-gsea}
run_gsea <- function(db) {
  members <- sets[startsWith(names(sets), paste0(db, "|"))]
  term_gene <- stack(members)[, c("ind", "values")]
  term_name <- select(filter(labels, database == db), set_id, label)
  set.seed(1)
  # GSEA() drops `...`, so eps never reaches enrichit and p below 1e-10 is floored with a warning.
  # The floored p reach no figure: the pathways come from 01, and colour is NES.
  suppressWarnings(compareCluster(
    ranked,
    fun = "GSEA", TERM2GENE = term_gene, TERM2NAME = term_name,
    minGSSize = 15, maxGSSize = 500, pvalueCutoff = 1, verbose = FALSE
  ))
}
compared <- map(set_names(unique(labels$database)), run_gsea)
```

## Check against 01

Join each set and leg's NES from this run to the fgsea NES in `set_tests`, and report the
correlation and the largest absolute difference per collection.

```{r check}
nes_check <- compared |>
  map(function(result) {
    transmute(
      as.data.frame(result),
      set_id = as.character(ID), contrast = arms[as.character(Cluster)], NES_08 = NES
    )
  }) |>
  list_rbind() |>
  inner_join(
    filter(set_tests, method == "fgsea") |> select(set_id, database, contrast, NES),
    by = c("set_id", "contrast")
  )
nes_check |>
  summarise(
    pairs = n(), r = cor(NES_08, NES), max_abs_diff = max(abs(NES_08 - NES)), .by = database
  )
```

## Draw figures

Every page carries an S-numbered caption. `caption()` takes the figure number, title, collection
and text, and returns the caption layer. `arm_fill` colours the two legs as in the other steps.

```{r figure-style}
caption <- function(number, title, db, text) {
  labs(caption = str_wrap(sprintf("S%d Figure. %s, %s. %s", number, title, db, text), 115))
}
arm_fill <- scale_fill_manual(values = c(BFR = "#B2182B", HLRT = "#2166AC"), name = NULL)
caption_theme <- theme(
  plot.caption = element_text(hjust = 0, size = 9, lineheight = 1.2),
  plot.caption.position = "plot"
)
source_note <- paste(
  "Pathways chosen from set_tests (01_run_fgsea_and_fry.xlsx): the collapse-surviving fgsea sets",
  "at FDR < 0.05 in either training contrast. NES and leading edges from the compareCluster run."
)
```

`maps()` draws a collection's four pages from `compared`. Pathway similarity is computed only among
the drawn pathways, since GO:BP holds 1,366 sets.

- S24, dotplot: BFR and HLRT side by side, colour NES (signed), dot
  size the share of the pathway in its leading edge, the proteins ranked before the running-sum
  peak.
- S25, enrichment map: a network with pathways as nodes, joined when their proteins overlap, each
  node a pie split by leg.
- S26, tree: pathways clustered by shared proteins, each cluster named by its most frequent words.
- S27, network: the five strongest pathways linked to their leading-edge proteins.

```{r maps}
maps <- function(db) {
  show <- filter(drawn, database == db)$label
  shown <- filter(compared[[db]], Description %in% show)
  similar <- pairwise_termsim(shown, showCategory = length(show))
  list(
    # dotplot logs its colour scale, built for p-values; NES is signed, so a diverging scale.
    dotplot(shown, showCategory = length(show), color = "NES", label_format = 45) +
      scale_fill_gradient2(low = "#2166AC", mid = "white", high = "#B2182B", name = "NES") +
      caption(24, "Pathways by leg", db, paste(
        "Colour is NES, dot size the share of the pathway in its leading edge.", source_note
      )),
    # On the two small collections (Hallmark, GO Slim) few pathways share proteins, and emapplot
    # warns from an internal max() over no edges; the map still draws.
    suppressWarnings(
      emapplot(similar, showCategory = length(show), label_format = 30, size_category = 1.6)
    ) + arm_fill +
      caption(25, "Enrichment map", db, paste(
        "Nodes are pathways, pies split by leg, joined when their proteins overlap.", source_note
      )),
    treeplot(
      similar,
      showCategory = length(show), nCluster = min(5, length(show) - 1), label_format = 32,
      fontsize_tiplab = 2.6, fontsize_cladelab = 2.6, hexpand = 0.5, cladelab_offset = 9
    ) + arm_fill +
      caption(26, "Pathway tree", db, paste(
        "Pathways clustered by shared proteins, each cluster named by its most frequent words.",
        source_note
      )),
    cnetplot(shown, showCategory = head(show, 5), node_label = "category") + arm_fill +
      caption(27, "Pathways and their proteins", db, paste(
        "The five strongest pathways and their leading-edge proteins; pies show which leg each",
        "protein leads in. Leading edges here come from the compareCluster run, so they can differ",
        "slightly from those in S21 of 07_leading_edge.", source_note
      ))
  ) |>
    map(function(p) p + caption_theme)
}
```

One A4 PDF per collection, four pages each.

```{r write-figures}
walk(unique(drawn$database), function(db) {
  pdf(file.path(stage, "b_reports", paste0("08_maps_", db, ".pdf")), width = 8.27, height = 11.69)
  walk(maps(db), print)
  invisible(dev.off())
})
```

## Summary

Pathways drawn per collection and leg, as the maps show them: how many of the drawn sets each
leg calls at FDR < 0.05.

```{r summary}
set_tests |>
  filter(method == "fgsea", contrast %in% arms, set_id %in% drawn$set_id) |>
  summarise(drawn = n(), fdr_05 = sum(padj < 0.05), .by = c(database, contrast))
```
